What is Interstellar Legends about?

Interstellar Legends takes you on a journey across the stars where teamwork, strategy and progression shape your rise to glory. Explore mysterious planets, uncover hidden gateways and expand your reach through challenging missions and rewarding discoveries. Lead a squad of unique heroes with elemental powers and rare abilities and face alien monsters in tactical turn-based battles. Victory depends on smart skill use, resource management and upgrading your crew with gear, microchips, and bio-cloning. Strategic team building lets you counter enemy strengths, while gateway challenges and epic boss encounters test your squad’s resilience. Every mission strengthens your heroes, every upgrade expands your power and every battle brings you closer to becoming a legend among the stars! Play more games on Y8 - The biggest modern HTML5 gaming platform!

How do we play Interstellar Legends?

You play Interstellar Legends entirely with your mouse — clicking to move through menus, select missions, manage inventory, and choose actions during battles.

What kind of game is Interstellar Legends?

Interstellar Legends is best described as a Sci-Fi Turn-Based RPG with Adventure and Strategy elements, enriched by MMO-style guilds and collections. It's played entirely with the mouse, making it accessible but layered with tactical depth.

Does Interstellar Legends rely more on strategy or quick thinking?

Interstellar Legends leans more toward quick thinking with a layer of strategy.

Because of the elemental system:

Earth > Water
Water > Fire
Fire > Wind
Wind > Earth
Chaos > Machine & Life
Life ↔ Machine (counter each other)

you do need basic strategy — knowing matchups and choosing the right element gives you a clear advantage.

However, in actual gameplay, success depends heavily on how fast you react:

Switching to the right element mid-fight
Responding to enemy attacks in real time
Adapting when opponents change elements

So while strategy sets you up, quick decision-making and reflexes are what win fights.

Who is Interstellar Legends for?

Interstellar Legends is designed for sci-fi fans who enjoy space exploration and futuristic themes. It appeals to RPG players who like leveling up, customizing gear, and engaging in tactical battles. It is also for casual MMO fans who want light guild and social features will also find it engaging.

What makes Interstellar Legends fun to play?

Interstellar Legends is fun because it combines galaxy exploration, squad-based turn‑based battles, deep upgrades like microchips and biocloning, and social features such as guilds and collections - giving players a lot to discover, fight, and progress through in a sci‑fi universe.

What is Pai Gow Poker about?

Pai Gow Poker is a fun online card game that combines the strategic elements of traditional poker with the distinct structure of the ancient Chinese game, Pai Gow. It offers an interesting blend of East and West, mixing the familiar aspects of poker hands with a domino-like gameplay. This results in a gaming experience that can be both challenging and exciting for card game enthusiasts. In Pai Gow Poker, the player is dealt seven cards from which they must form two separate poker hands - one consisting of five cards and another of two cards. The objective is to beat both of the dealer's corresponding hands. The strategic aspect of the game lies in determining the best way to arrange the seven cards into two hands without knowing how the dealer will separate their cards. This can be done in just one round or two or more rounds by making consecutive part-scores whose contract score add up to 100 points or more. When the rubbers is completed both teams compare their total points with higher score deciding the winner. Each round is divided into two main parts: bidding and play. After the hands are dealt, each team bets on how many tricks they think can win based on their hand strength and the suits available. A bid includes a number 1-1 and a trump suit. GAME DETAILS
What is Mahjongg Titans about?

Mahjong Solitaire is one of the most popular board games in the world, and Mahjongg Titans stays true to its core mechanics. The goal is to remove all tiles from the board by matching pairs of identical tiles. Only free tiles can be selected. A free tile is one that is not covered by another tile and has at least one open side on the left or right. This rule encourages careful planning and smart decision making.
At the beginning of the game, the board may look complex, with tiles stacked in multiple layers. As you remove matching pairs, new tiles become available, opening up fresh possibilities. Choosing the right matches in the right order is important, because removing tiles too quickly or without planning can block future moves. This balance between simplicity and strategy is what makes Mahjongg Titans engaging.
The visual style is clean and traditional. The tiles feature familiar Mahjong symbols such as characters, bamboo, circles, winds, and seasons. Everything is clearly visible, allowing you to focus fully on matching tiles without distractions. The background is subtle and calm, supporting a relaxed atmosphere that suits the pace of the game.
Mahjongg Titans is designed to be played at your own speed. There is no pressure to rush, which makes it ideal for short breaks or longer sessions when you want to relax and think through each move. The game rewards patience, observation, and careful planning rather than quick reactions.
Because the rules are easy to learn, Mahjongg Titans is welcoming for new players. At the same time, the layered layouts provide enough challenge to keep experienced Mahjong players interested. Clearing large sections of the board feels satisfying, and completing the full layout gives a strong sense of accomplishment.
If you enjoy classic tile matching games with simple rules and a relaxing pace, Mahjongg Titans delivers a timeless Mahjong experience that you can enjoy again and again.

Bloxd.io is an IO adventure game with Minecraft-style visuals where you can navigate obstacle courses, gather resources, craft tools, battle other players, and much more. With game modes ranging from parkour challenges and creative sandbox building to combat-based gameplay, there's something for every playstyle.

How to Play Bloxd.io

The best way to start playing Bloxd.io is to gather wood, your most essential early resource and useful even in caves. Kill sheep early to collect 3 wool and craft a bed, which gives you a 15-minute speed boost to help you explore faster.

Follow this progression to get established: gather wood and craft a workbench, then mine stone for a stone pickaxe. From there, find iron ore, smelt it in a furnace, and craft an iron pickaxe. You'll need at least iron to mine diamonds.

Game Modes

BloxdHop.io: Race to the end of the map before time runs out by hopping parkour-style across blocks of all shapes and sizes.

DoodleCube: Similar to Gartic.io, players build objects based on a given theme while others vote on how well they match it.

EvilTower: Climb to the top of the Evil Tower using your parkour skills. Inspired by the Tower of Hell, it's a serious test of patience and precision.

Peaceful: A creative, pressure-free mode where you roam freely, collect resources, and build whatever you like.

CubeWarfare: Compete against other players in a third-person shooter where building blocks are part of the strategy.

Bloxd.io is regularly updated with new features and modes. Other available modes include Survival, Creative, Bedwars, Sky Wars, OneBlock, Greenville, Hide and Seek, Murder Mystery, Plots, Pirates, Survival Royale, and Worlds.

Look for biomes with spiky black or carved stone formations, which are a strong indicator that diamonds are nearby. Check the tips and tops of the spike towers, not just the base. Skull-shaped structures sometimes contain chests worth looting as well.

Hold off on diamond armor until you have 30 or more diamonds, as a full set costs 24. Aim for Protection III enchantments before jumping into PvP, and craft a diamond pickaxe for more efficient mining. Secure your base first before spending diamonds on gear.

Tips

Pickaxes in Bloxd.io have unlimited durability, so one iron pickaxe goes a long way
Use homes strategically — set one at your base and another near enemy bases or resource-rich areas
Avoid fighting mobs and players with unenchanted armor — you can take massive damage in a single hit
Don't hoard junk items; keep your inventory clean for valuable resources

Piece of Cake: Merge and Bake is a puzzle casual game where you help Emily, the main character, breathe new life into her family’s rundown cafe while uncovering long-lost family secrets. Solve a variety of challenging puzzles, manage the cafe's operations, and craft creative item combinations to unlock new chapters of the story. As you progress, enjoy heartwarming moments and unexpected twists that keep you engaged at every turn.

How to Play Piece of Cake: Merge and Bake

In Piece of Cake: Merge and Bake, your goal is to merge matching items to create new ones until the board is cleared of all matches. Start by clicking on the toast pan to make toast. Merge two pieces of toast to get toast with a sunny-side-up egg, and continue merging upgraded items like salami, sandwiches, and beyond. Each new combination helps you progress through the game.

As you complete customer orders by matching the correct items, you'll earn money to restore the café and other locations around town. Each renovation reveals more of the town's hidden story, making your progress both satisfying and intriguing. The game's beautiful graphics and detailed animations make every step feel rewarding.

The puzzles are fun and very addictive, pushing you to think strategically as you merge as many items as possible. How to Play Mahjongg Solitaire

Spot the patterns

Mahjong is a tricky puzzle game. There are so many tiles, many of which look the same but feature slight differences. Along with the need to spot these patterns, you can’t move any pieces with both sides blocked. The left or right side needs to be accessible, at least.

Finding a couple of “free” tiles is the challenge here, with a tile-free being when there are no tiles on top of it. In addition, either its left or right side needs to be open. In this version of Mahjong Solitaire, you can look at the top of your screen to understand how many pairs of tiles are “free” to be matched, plus you can match the special tiles, those with a colored background, anytime.

Use hints when you’re stuck

Mahjongg Solitaire features hints if you get stuck, but unlike some other mahjong games, it does not have a shuffle feature. The games are also timed, meaning there is some urgency to how many tiles you can match.

When the game ends, you’ll get a score for the tiles you matched and a bonus for how far you got in the game before your time ran out.

Tile groups in Mahjongg Solitaire

Mahjongg Solitaire features 144 tiles divided primarily into three suits. The primary suits are:

Dots - feature circles
Bamboo - feature lines
Characters - feature Chinese characters

In Mahjongg Solitaire, you’ll also notice special tiles that can be matched even without the same image. These are highlighted in blue or green.

Openfront.io is an IO battle game where you expand your territory, build up your economy, forge alliances, and drop bombs to dominate the map.

How to Play Openfront

Before jumping in, you'll choose how you want to play. You can dive into a solo game, create a private lobby, or join an existing one. From there, you pick your map. The selection is massive:

Large-scale maps cover regions like the World, North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Africa, and Oceania
Regional maps get more specific with options like Britannia, Japan, Italy, Iceland, the Strait of Gibraltar, the Amazon River, the Gulf of St. Lawrence, New York City, East Asia, Australia, and many more
Fantasy and alternate maps include Pangaea, Mars, Pluto, Deglaciated Antarctica, and arcade maps like Didier and Sierpinski
Or just hit Random and see where you land

Difficulty options range from Easy all the way up to Impossible, so there's a setting for every skill level.

Tabs & Settings

Play is where you launch into a game
News keeps you updated on developer patches, bug fixes, and new features
Leaderboard shows ranked data for individual players and clans, including games played, wins, and losses
Settings lets you pick your flag, toggle special effects, choose territory skins, enable emojis, and set your default attack ratio so you're not adjusting the slider every time you spawn

Getting Started

When you start the game, pick your starting location and begin claiming the empty territory around you. The map has three terrain types: plains, highlands, and mountains. Each one gets progressively harder to capture, so factor that into where you spawn. Your control panel sits in the bottom left and includes an attack slider that controls what percentage of your troops you send out. Keep an eye on your population bar, too. Green means your population is growing, yellow means it's shrinking, and growth peaks at around 41% of your max population.

Who You'll Run Into

As you expand, you'll start bumping into three types of entities. Bots are the weakest and can't build anything. Nations are NPC factions that can build infrastructure and launch bombs. Players are your real competition. You can form alliances with any of them, but if you betray an ally, you'll take a defense debuff for 30 seconds, so choose your moments carefully.

Infrastructure

Buildings are the backbone of your strategy:

Cities increase your max population by 25k
Ports generate trade ships that grow your economy and let you build warships for attacking and raiding
Factories connect cities and ports via train networks, generating gold with every run, especially when trading with neighbors and allies
Defense posts fortify your borders and slow enemy pushes
SAM launchers protect a small area from incoming nukes, and leveling them up increases their range
Missile silos let you launch nuclear weapons

Most buildings can be stacked to level them up, which works the same as having multiple copies of that building in different locations.

Nuclear Weapons

Atom bombs are small and precise, best used against specific targets
Hydrogen bombs cover a much wider area and deal serious population damage
MIRVs are the big ones, blanketing enemy territory with a spread of missiles

How to Play Four Colors

There are various strategies you can use to maximize your chances of winning at this multiplayer UNO-inspired game. The main principle is to get rid of all your cards before everyone else. You can do that by matching the color or number of the card placed down before yours. If you don't have a playable card, you must draw cards from the pile until you do.

When you have one card left, press the "1" button; otherwise, you will be punished with two penalty cards!

Number cards

There are 108 cards and four colors in total. Number cards make up 70% of the total deck, with four colors each containing 19 cards. The cards span from numbers 0-9. As for the quantity of each card, there is one zero card and two of every other number. The remaining 30% of cards are called action cards and wild cards.

Action cards

Action cards add an extra level of strategy to UNO. There are three action card types in a UNO deck. There are two of each action card in each color. These are:

Skip card - the next player in the sequence misses a turn.
Reverse - reverses the direction of play.
Draw two - the next player draws two cards and misses one turn.
Wild cards

There are two types of wildcards, with four of each one. They are:

Wild - lets the player choose what color to play.
Wild draw 4 - declare the next color to match, and force the next player to draw four cards.

UNO is a card game developed by Merle Robbins in 1971. He sold the rights to the game for $50,000 to a company that was bought out by Mattel in 1992.

Over the years, it's grown to become one of the most recognizable card games. There are now 100s of themed variations of the game based on anything from football to movies, some with slightly different rules and special cards.

There are two layers of tiles stacked on top of each other in War Mahjong. Your goal is to clear tiles that are the same and beside each other until all the tiles have disappeared. Magic Mahjong: A Classic Puzzle in an Epic Fantasy Battle!

Forget about peaceful solitaire! Magic Mahjong is a hybrid of classic Mahjong and strategic fantasy combat. Here, your observation, logic, and strategic thinking determine the outcome of an epic clash.

How to Play

It's all about your approach: the core mechanic is simple, find and remove matching tiles to clear the pyramid. From there, you decide whether it becomes a relaxing game of classic Mahjong or a strategic battle where every removed pair is a calculated move that shifts the balance of power on the battlefield.

Every symbol on a tile is a spell. By matching pairs, you don't just clear the board, you directly influence the tide of battle:

Attack: Unleash elemental spells of fire, lightning, and ice. The more matching symbols in a pair, the more powerful the strike! One symbol hits a single target, while nine unleashes a devastating area-of-effect attack.
Defense: Heal your hero and erect protective barriers.
Control: Slow, immobilize, or weaken entire enemy squads, dramatically altering the course of the fight.
Your Secret Weapon: the "Refresh" Button!

How to Play
Basic Solitaire rules

The rules of Solitaire are simple, but it can be a tricky game to master. The objective is to successfully remove all the cards from the playing field by placing them in number order by their respective suit.

Move the visible cards around to create a complete set in order from King to Ace. The cards must be placed in the same suit, in numerical order. If you cannot move any card, you need to click the pile of cards that is face down to add a new card to each row. If you are stuck, you can always use the reset button to start from scratch! Can you master Spider Solitaire 2 Suits?

Spider Solitaire rules

Unlike basic Solitaire, Spider Solitaire is trickier. It features two decks of cards and 10 rows. Playing with only two suits ramps up the difficulty even further. Other than these limitations, the rules are the same as regular Solitaire. You must stack cards of the same suit in descending order on the tableau. You’ll win the game when all the cards have been put in order.

About this game

This simple Spider Solitaire 2 Suits game features a clean, retro interface. There are no hints, so you should be experienced at playing Spider Solitaire before jumping into this one. However, you can undo your previous moves or completely reset the game when you get stuck.

Solitaire Home Story is a puzzle card game where you play through multiple levels of the solitaire card game, which helps you unlock home renovations as you slowly unfold the dramatic story set in the town of Brook's End.

How to Play Solitaire Home Story

You play as Alice, who has just returned to her childhood home with her friend Tara, a few years after her mom passed away, only to find the place in terrible shape. The house is damaged, potentially on fire, and her dad is nowhere to be found. Making things worse, if Alice cannot get the ranch fixed up in time, the town mayor will have it torn down. The story unfolds as you play through solitaire rounds, with each game you complete helping repair and clean up a portion of the house.

Alice discovers through Tara that her dad has fallen into some shady dealings while struggling on his own since her mom passed. Things take a darker turn when Alice finds a threatening note and a knife inside the house, making it clear her dad is in danger. The mystery of where he has gone drives the narrative forward as you keep completing rounds. After all the tension and buildup, you eventually find him safe in the basement, where it turns out he had been searching for Oscar's dog bed the entire time.

The Core Card Game

The solitaire mechanic is straightforward. There is a base card displayed at the bottom of the screen, and your job is to tap cards from the layout that are one value higher or one value lower than that base card. For example, if the base card is a 7, you can play a 6 or an 8. That played card then becomes the new base, and you continue chaining up or down from there. If you get stuck and have no playable cards available, tap the deck to draw a new base card and keep going.

As you get more comfortable with the chaining mechanic, you can aim for streaks by clearing five cards in a row without tapping the deck. Pulling off a streak earns you reward bonuses that help you progress faster through the story.

Joker cards act as wildcards that you can use when you are stuck. Beyond that, the game offers a variety of boosters you can deploy to smash through tougher levels. You will also run into blockers that shake things up, like mischievous squirrels that block your cards from being played. Tools like wrecking balls can clear the entire board when things get out of hand. Each new level tends to introduce a fresh twist, so no two rounds feel the same.

Home Renovation

Between card games, the story gives you tasks to complete around the house. You can check your current to-do list by tapping on the table in the game. Completing solitaire rounds clears tasks and unlocks new parts of the house to restore. The renovation side of the game lets you act as a designer, choosing new rugs, floors, furniture, and more to transform each room. As you progress, you unlock additional spaces like the veranda, the spa, and the library, each of which hides deeper family mysteries to uncover.

Characters You Will Meet

Alice is not on her own throughout the journey. Her friend Tara is there with her from the start, and she quickly reunites with Oscar the dog. She also meets Dee Dee, a mischievous lamb, and Jako, a talkative macaw. Along the way, she encounters quirky characters, including her dad, Lavinia, a mystical fortune-teller, and Nate, her childhood crush. The game weaves relationship building and a few secrets worth keeping into the story alongside all the card gameplay.

Kings and Queens Solitaire TriPeaks is a casual puzzle solitaire game whose objective is to stack all cards on the game table in sequence. This game is ideal for card players, especially solitaire fans, as it is intuitive to pick up quickly with similar solitaire gameplay but with a slight twist—cards are not in laid out the same way, suits don't matter and rank order can go from high to low to high again!

How to Play Kings and Queens Solitaire TriPeaks

The aim of the game is to match cards by rank. Tap a card that is either one rank higher or lower than the card you are working from. For example, if you have a 5, you can play a 6 or a 4. This sequence can continue in either direction (e.g., 4 → 5 → 6 or 6 → 5 → 4).

The Table Setup

The game begins with a dynamic layout of cards on the table, blending uncovered cards. You can play with covered cards waiting to be revealed. Your objective is to build sequences using only the uncovered cards, so strategize carefully to unlock new possibilities.

At the bottom of the game board, you’ll find your home base card, the foundation of your sequences. Every move you make starts here, guiding your progress through the game. Next to your home base is the deck of cards, your lifeline when you run out of moves on the table. Draw from this deck to refresh your strategy and keep the game moving forward.

Pay close attention to how the cards are arranged, and start planning your moves to reveal hidden opportunities and outsmart the deck!

Suits don’t matter, so you can match cards regardless of their suit, focusing solely on their numerical value.

The key to winning is to strategize your moves. It’s often best to start with a lower-numbered card so you have more flexibility to build sequences. Aim to clear as many cards as possible with each move by carefully planning increases and decreases (e.g., a sequence like 4 → 5 → 4 → 6 removes multiple cards).

If no moves are available, you will be prompted to draw a card from the deck. The card you draw becomes the new card you must build from. If no uncovered cards are playable, you’ll also need to draw from the deck.

The game becomes more challenging as you go. Occasionally, you may receive prompts to add five more cards to the table, increasing the difficulty. If you make a move you regret, use the Undo button to revise your strategy.

Kings and Queens Solitaire TriPeaks Tip

If you have several sequence options, prioritize moves that remove the most cards from the table or deck. For example, a sequence like 4 → 5 → 4 → 6 can clear more cards than a straight increase like 4 → 5 → 6.

Magic Towers Solitaire is a free solitaire game with a medieval theme. Move all the cards from the three peaks back to the deck. Remove all the cards to move to the next round!

How to Play
Remove cards from the tableau

Magic Towers Solitaire is a unique solitaire game, also known as Three Towers Solitaire and Tri-Peaks Solitaire. Your objective is to move all the cards from the three peaks back to the deck and complete as many rounds as possible. The game ends when you have no moves left.

Place the cards in sequence

Move the next card in the sequence to the deck in ascending or descending order. The card can be any suit, as long as it is the next card in the sequence, i.e., 4-5-6 or 6-5-4. You can move up and down the sequence as much as you like, i.e., 4-5-6-5-6-5-4.

If none of the available cards meet these criteria, you can take another card from the pile of face-down cards. There’s also a wild card that can be used at any time.

More Games Like This

There are many more free solitaire games available to play at CrazyGames. If you want a good recommendation, try Classic Solitaire. For another type of popular card game, check out Uno Online.

You have the option to undo the previous move or use the wild card you stored.

Yes, this variant of solitaire goes by a few different names.

Golf Solitaire is a fun and challenging solo card game. Clear all the cards by placing them in order and returning them to the pile until none are remaining. This game uses a regular 52-card deck, but the rules differ from regular Solitaire.

How to Play Golf Solitaire

The objective of Golf Solitaire is to get all cards from the seven columns into the single face-up pile at the bottom. Cards can be moved to this pile if they are one number higher or lower than the top card.

When there are no cards to play, you can flip a card from the face-down pile until you get one that can be played.

How do I win?

You win the game when you successfully move all the cards from the seven columns into your face-up pile. The game is lost when you get stuck with no more cards left to play.

However, there are hints and a "card steal" button for when you're stuck. Steal takes a card from one of the columns at random, regardless of what it is. The hint button will show you the best move when there are moves available.

More Solitaire Games

Solo card games are a popular way to pass the time and stimulate the mind when at home. Try out something popular like Uno Online. You could also try Pyramid Solitaire Ancient Egypt - clear the pyramid of cards by pairing cards that add up to 13.

The theme of the Jam is simply "BINGO". 


We have combined the mechanism of Pachinko Slot machine and classic dungeon crawler.  We have named our game "Fate Machine".

Place your bet and pull the lever, your fate is up to the slot machine as your HP is your betting chips. There are total of 4 different types of slot symbols, each symbols have high/low version, which means they represent higher bet return:

RED: Physical attack

BLUE: Magical Attack

YELLOW: Faith, with enough faith you could engage free spin without any betting cost

PURPLE: Discovery, return you equipment that improve you stats.

Each colour also return WILDS, which is a wild card for your slot colour.

The goal of the game is to simple survive as long as you can in the dungeon, deal damage to your foe and replensih your betting energy in the altar every 10 rounds. 

The game have light Roguelike elements, in which after you died the game will not end, you could use the loot you gathered in the dungeon to upgrade your campsite, improving your combat effectiveness in the dungeon.

Six Match

This is a rare kind of Match 3 game. Move Mr Swap With Coins to swap places with coins. You must make a match within 6 moves.


Survival Mode

Match coins of the same type to create a poker hand for extra points. Gems do not match, they are collected when they hit the bottom row.  Other mechanics are added as you play.

You get 3 hints for free to show you the ropes. Then you have 6 more that will only appear if you press the Help button. If no hint is available, the help button creates a bomb. After your last Help is gone, you must figure it out or cash in what's left.

Six Match auto-saves your game. A game can last for weeks, take your time.

Puzzle Mode

Clear the board of coins in these bite size challenges.

Keys:

W,A,S,D or cursor keys to move
Space or Z to press help button in Survival Mode
Space or Z to undo in Puzzle Mode
X to redo in Puzzle Mode
Esc to open menu

I've not encountered a no-hints bug. The solver sometimes takes up to 30 seconds to solve the board, though the hint button will appear after 8 seconds if it solves sooner. Are you sure you waited long enough? If it happens again and you're able to save a screenshot (imgur.com will host it for free) it would help me a lot in tracking it down.

I don't want to create a trade between score and hints - I've considered it, but the conversation that happens in your head when you play this game is crucial to its appeal ("oh no I'm dead, oh wait, yes, I'M ALIVE!"). The hints already soften this, but keep the tension ramped up. If you could always buy your way out of failure, you'd never feel the full-force-rush of figuring a way out of what you thought was death. You wouldn't push yourself as hard.

The end-game does need some work though - so there's some more mechanics and adjustments yet to come. I may implement a way to get more hints, but I want you to work for it and feel proud of yourself when you achieve it.

HOW TO PLAY POKÉSLOTS
THE BASICS

1. Spin & Catch
Click SPIN to rotate the reels.

Match 3: If you land on three of the same Pokémon, you catch it!
Evolution Jackpot: If you land on a full evolution line (e.g., Charmander → Charmeleon → Charizard), you get a massive Coin payout.
Shiny Hunting: Keep your eyes peeled for sparkles. Shiny Pokémon are rare (1-in-20 chance), but capturing one adds it to your Shiny Dex.

2. Explore the World
Use your Coins to unlock new Biomes (Forests, Caves, Oceans).

Each Biome contains different Pokémon.
Check your Pokedex often—if you have gaps, try traveling to a different location!
BOSS BATTLES (New in v3.0!)

Once you have caught every standard Pokémon in a region, the SPIN button will transform into a red BATTLE button. You must defeat the Mythical Boss (Mew, Celebi, Jirachi) to unlock the next Game Cartridge.

Combat Rules:
The reels change from Pokémon to Battle Icons.

⚔️ Sword: Deals damage to the Boss.
🛡️ Shield: You take recoil damage, but you block the Boss's massive attack.
🧪 Potion: Heals your HP.

Tip: If you lose, don't worry! You can try again immediately.

THE BUDDY SYSTEM

Go to your Pokédex and click on any Pokémon you have caught to set it as your Buddy.

Your Buddy appears in the glass pod on the main screen.
Watch the Pod: When a 🎁 icon appears, click your buddy to claim a reward (Coins, Rare Candies, or Buffs).
Evolution: If you find a Rare Candy, your Buddy might evolve into its next form!
SYSTEM MENU
SHOP: Spend excess coins on cosmetic upgrades like Console Skins, Button Styles, and Reel Designs.
CARTRIDGES: Switch between Kanto (Gen 1), Johto (Gen 2), and Hoenn (Gen 3) once you unlock them.
CLOUD SAVE: Create a username/password to sync your progress across devices.
Note: No email verification required. Just remember your password!
 SECRETS & EASTER EGGS

There are hidden modes and a notoriously famous glitch Pokémon buried in the code.

Ruins of Alph: Rumor has it there is a secret way to enter the Ruins if you have the right Pokémon in your Dex...
Glitches: Not everything in Pallet Town is as stable as it seems... 
CONTROLS
Mouse/Touch: Click buttons to interact.
Double-Click: Used for certain secret interactions in the Pokédex.
Mobile Friendly: The game automatically resizes for vertical phone screens.

Probably Poker is a card game probably similar to your average round of video poker. Its key difference being that the remaining suits pullable from each round's deck are revealed to you ahead of time; use that information however your liking.


There's also some health management and extra difficulty you've got to contend with. The dealer can deduct quite large sums of money from you if they happen to get a good hand; I hope you don't find it too daunting... The game will end in your defeat if you run out of either cash or hearts! Please be careful. 

I've been working on this on/off for awhile now. It's the first game I collaborated with other people on for additional resources like art and music, so it finally getting finished is a decently big deal to me despite its small-scale. Such wonderful people involved include:

Texas Lane'em Poker
a gambling game for the 3 Lane Card Game Jam 22 by Arnold Rauers.

Goal

Play Texas Hold'em Poker on 3 different lanes against the dealer. Win hands to gain enough chips for the next rounds buy in. How many rounds can you survive?

Interaction

At the start of the turn redraw or hold your hand cards. Click a lanes draw pile to draw the next card. Click the "Cash In" button to complete a round. Collect your payout to start the next round.

Lane Actions

Each lane has a randomized action which triggers once you've drawn the lanes "eye" card. These actions will introduce randomness to the standard poker system and can work out in your favor or against you. Think about how far you want to push your luck with each draw.

Hand Strength

The % value of each lanes hand is the relative strength of your current hand in that lane. 100% would mean a Royal Flush with clubs.

Disclaimer: This game was made in about a week and will contain major bugs and issues!

Note that the web version is a work in progress.  Most of the features have been ported over, but the  hand history UI screens from the original Cocos2dx Windows version have not been yet.  These features will be added in the web version in the near future.

Summary

Play Texas Hold'em multi-table tournament poker with fake chips against a variety of AI opponents with configurable tournament settings and AI play style. This is a poker simulation game for serious poker players. Opponents can even "go on tilt" after bad beats just like real players would! Game pauses dramatically during all-in situations with displayed percentages, and you can advance the action card by card!  View your hand history to review past hands in the tournament and also review past opponent actions and cards that were revealed during play.  

The game automatically saves your progress during each action in the hand so you can select "Continue" when starting the game again to pick back up where you left off.

The game also has a "perks system" where winning hands will fill a meter where you can peek at N cards based on the green number in the lower left.  You can use this to preview future community cards or reveal other opponent cards.  This can be ignored or disabled in the settings if desired.

This game was heavily inspired by the old BioTools "Poker Academy" training software from the mid-2000s.  I logged 100ks hands on this software, and it really taught me to play better along with the awesome community that was behind it. Some of the AI play styles were inspired by this game.




AI Opponents




Depending on difficulty selected, the tournament will be seeded with a variety of opponents of different play styles.  Players can be configured to "go on tilt" just like real players would if they suffer a bad beat.  This causes opponents to behave sub-optimally for a period after such an occurrence.  The wild card ones will be a minority of players, but just like in a real tournament there will be a few players doing all kinds of crazy things :) 

Opponent Type	Play Style
Optimal	Uses fuzzy logic  to play hands like I would in different tournament situations.
Adaptive Evaluator	Uses expected value and tracks player tendencies and shown hands to put players on hands and use expected value on hand simulations to evaluate call/raise/fold actions.
Default Evaluator	Similar to above but only considers fixed probabilities when determining expected value of actions and not player tendencies.
Jam	This uses a strategy developed by professional poker player David Sklansky for amateur players where the decision on each hand pre-flop is all-in or fold based on hole card strength.
Raising	An extreme personality that will play a variety of hands and will always raise or fold and never call.  
Calling Station	An extreme passive personality that will always limp into pots pre-flop and check/call a variety of hands and chase draws.  The typical fish opponent.
Random	A wildcard opponent that will always raise premium hands but then will also take a random raise/call/fold approach to everything else!  You never know if he's got it but he often will not.
Chase Draw	Plays like the optimal opponent for all but straight and flush draws, which they will chase relentlessly often to their own demise.




Future of the Game

The Godot web version of the game is the current focus.  I will continue to port the game features from the Cocos2dx version into the web version and enhance the overall experience.

Thanks for checking out Scrongly!

Scrongly is a poker themed roguelike deckbuilder, wherein your objective is to play good poker hands. The better hands you play, the more points you get.

Each round you will have a certain score threshold to reach. It starts off at a paltry 300, but quickly escalates into millions! Don't run out of cards in your deck before reaching the score threshold, or your run is over!

Luckily, after each round you can spend chips you earn to purchase new cards, including some you won't see in a typical deck! You can also purchase Zodiacs, which improve the score you receive from different hands, like full houses or straight flushes (and any hands including that hand). Most excitingly, you can purchase Baubles, which improve your run in very different ways.

Try finding powerful combinations of Baubles, cards and Zodiacs to reach the highest round you can!




*** How to play ***

You can play Scrongly with a mouse, or a controller!

Start by pressing "Play" on the main menu, then press "Standard Game". You can pick a deck here, but if its your first time playing, you only have access to the default deck. Press "Play" again to start.

If using a mouse, you can either click and drag cards into the play zone, or click on up to five cards to select them, then click the "Play" button, or on the play zone to deposit them there. With a controller, navigate to the cards you want to play and select the with the south button, then press "Play", or the north button. You can also move cards around by holding down the south button with one selected, then using the left stick directions to rearrange them. Once you're satisfied with your hand, press the Lock button to lock in your hand.

You can also select up to five cards and click "Discard" if you don't like your hand. Be warned: you have a limited number of discards.

You also have a limited number of hands you can lock in before you become "Fatigued". Once Fatigued, you will discard all remaining cards in your hand after locking in a hand, making it very difficult to put together strong hands. Keep an eye on the counters on the left side of the screen, which display your remaining discards and hands until fatigue.

Once you reach the round's score threshold, you will be taken to the shop, where you can purchase new cards, Zodiacs and Baubles to improve your run. Spend chips you earned during the ante, and don't be stingy! The game ramps up in difficulty quickly.

*** Tips ***

-  Non-standard cards (ones without a rank and suit) do not take up space in your hand

- Zodiacs improve all hands that contain the hand of the zodiac. For example, the One Pair zodiac will improve Three of a Kind, Full House, and Four of a Kind. Higher tier hands affect a more narrow range of hands, and scale better

- With a hand placed, mouse over the "Hands" tag on the left side of the screen (or press  to see exactly what hands are contained in your played hand

- You can adjust the game speed in  "Menu" -> "Gameplay". You can also switch to a dark theme there

Silver Dubloons

(1 edit)

Thanks for the feedback! I don't think anything changed to affect the rarity of those Baubles, but I have had the same thought that I wished they were more common! Currently the way an item is generated in the shop goes like this:

If there is a Bauble of each rarity available, add that rarity to the pool of possible rarities, then generate a number between 0 and all available rarities weights combined. If it is less than the common weight, generate a random common Bauble from the list of available ones. If it is less than common weight plus uncommon, generate a random uncommon, and so on.

I've been thinking that perhaps the number of available Baubles should influence the weight, as in changing that formula to be generating a number between 0 and (common weight * available common Baubles) + (common weight * available uncommon Baubles) etc.

Since there are so many rare Baubles (one for each hand plus more) this may have the desired effect, with a bonus of being able to increase the odds of certain rarities by buying out Baubles, like once you buy the slap bracelet Bauble you'll be less likely to see uncommon Baubles.

There's downsides to this system, too, like most common Baubles can be bought many times so it may end up increasing the number of Commons found, maybe I'd have to tinker with the weights to test this system out.

There's my thoughts for now, I'd happily take any feedback on my methodology or any thoughts you've had on how you'd change it too!

Thanks again and have a great day!

Edit - oh and you can also make a custom game and change the weights of Bauble rarities in the custom game menu (special button). That might be worth tinkering around with to find a balance that you like!

Poker-man is a mix of Arcade and Poker,  created during the Ludum Dare 41 Game jam, with the theme: Combine 2 Incompatible Genres.




The goal is to defeat the 4 enemies with poker or blackjack hand.


How ?

By collecting the best poker hand possible then run into the enemy you think you are gonna beat.




You can also play with Blackjack rules, trying to get a sum of 21 without going over !













 Careful, you can only see the first two cards of an enemy's hand.




If your hand is weaker than the enemy, you will lose the minimum bet amount  




or the amount you personally bet. You can bet more than the minimum when you think have a good hand.




If you lose all your money, it’s game over.

You can attack without risk any enemy that doesn’t have any card if you have at least one card.

page_title: I hardly know'er - Poker Idler Prototype by Chatex
text:
View all by Chatex
Follow Chatex
Add To Collection
Related games
Run game

Gameplay prototype. Looking for feedback on whether the loop works.

None of the art, gameplay, content , or much of anything is FINAL yet. This is a pre-alpha vertical slice prototype.

Note: The game starts with a bit of a forced loss to introduce the player to the "shove" which is the main prestige mechanic and way to get persistent upgrades. Purchase the poker poster from the catalog on the shove screen to play normally. A How to Play page also opens on a new game, and you can reopen it any time with the ? button in the top right.

How to play

 Hands resolve automatically no poker knowledge required; just click the deal button and hopefully watch bankroll tick up over time. If you're off to a bad start might just want to shove to start a new run.
Open more tables to grind faster. Watch your focus: running more tables than your capacity drags your per-hand value down on every table.
Opening a table costs its buy-in, this gets subtracted from your bankroll and added to the table.
There are 4 different game-types that play differently - 
6-max is vanilla
Heads up is harder to win, faster hands and more Stack wins AND losses
Zoom is fastest, with the smallest pots
MTT is a 8 hand tournament, Make it to hands 6,7,8 to cash, a full sweep of 8 banks a guaranteed Gold Chip
Spend bankroll on run upgrades (reset on shove) or buyins for more tables. 
Win a Stack (the biggest win tier) to bank Gold Chips for that table, once per stake/type each run. Gold Chips are the meta/prestige currency.
When you've pushed the run as far as it'll go, shove.  Your shove win % is shown before you commit, and is calculated by your base shove % and bankroll multiplier (more bankroll, more base %, higher chance to win all in)
Win or lose, you prestige. Keep your Gold Chips, spend them in the catalog for permanent upgrades, grind again.
Cursors are the idle loop, unlocked in the catalog (Box of Mice).
Expected value is shown at the bottom of each table, hover over it for detailed info (how many big blinds you can expect to win/lose per hand on average). The gold % next to it is your chance to hit a Stack.

The goal of the prototype is to get enough shove% to win the shove.

What I want feedback on

Anything that reads as a bug.
Does the grind hold for the playtime and how is the pace (30-60 min roughly for content present)
What would you like to see added or anything that doesn't make sense/detracts?
Any other feedback. Be as detailed as you like, what you like or didn't, etc

Controls

Mouse only. Space, esc, and enter do some very minor UI related stuff like continue or quit. Spam space to get through the SHOVE faster (skip animations).

Built in

LÖVE2d and Lua

Cards faces: FREE Pixel Art Playing Cards by KereneL

Card backs: Microsoft Solitaire's Artwork: Revisited by kid marscat

MTT is trash except for just getting the PP for unlock after shoving.

Zoeti is a turn-based roguelike that features a deck of playing cards used to create card combos and activate skills in the heat of battle. Bolster your arsenal of skills through battles, discoverable upgrades, or aid from the locals which enhance your plays to overcome the evil plaguing your land.

A once peaceful land, now overrun by monsters. You, a Star-Soul hero, are among a select few blessed to raze the land of evil.

In Zoeti, you are equipped with a deck of playing cards, with which you play card combinations (pair, full house, royal flush, etc.) to activate skills that will attack or defend against enemies. Further bolster your arsenal of skills and upgrades through battles and discovery.

The blood of a dead god congeals into monsters roaming the countryside, threatening devout townsfolk and the simple lives they lead. Will you, a Star-Soul hero, protect them from the ravages of evil? In Zoeti, you'll need to crack open the enemy's defenses, bolster your grit and resolve, all while outsmarting the underhanded foes you face. Use your deck of playing cards to activate skills, attack foes, and defend yourself with card combinations, such as two pair, a full house, or straight flush. Through battle, discovery, and clever decision-making, you'll upgrade and enhance your build to complete the toughest challenges Zoeti has to offer.

 Characters: 




Valentina 

An honorable knight dedicated to protecting the weak and standing as a bulwark against evil, Valentina blocks incoming attacks with her stalwart shield and puts the might of raw muscle behind every sword swing. Play Valentina if you like outlasting opponents, meeting them head on with pulverizing power. 




Alves

 An elusive trickster, Alves knows how to hamstring her enemies' quickest attacks, evade their most devastating blows, and make them bleed for every swing they take. Play Alves if you like outsmarting opponents with clever ploys and deadly combos. 




Nicora 

An ingenius mage, Nicora combines the raw power of elemental fire, ice and lightning to burn, freeze and shock her opponents into submission. Play Nicora if harnessing the primal power of terrifying magic seems the best way to defeat the trial of the gods.

 Features: 


A Royal Flush - Every ability is associated with a poker hand; the more complex the hand, the more impactful the ability!
Create a Powerful Arsenal - Upgrade, purchase, or quest for new skills for your runs. Discover new synergies to overcome your opposition and create mechanically rich strategies.
Your Choices Have Consequences - Risk everything on a tough fight with an exceptional reward or take the easy path to guarantee victory.
Meet Fuzzy Friends - From Winfred the cheerful innkeeper with a powerful secret to Rabelle, the devious scoundrel just as likely to trick you as to help you.
Endless Possibilities - Three different game modes playable with three different characters at five different difficulties featuring dozens of different builds and hundreds of different enemies... Every run is unique!

Welcome to The Golden Caravan, kid. A place where fortunes are made, loyalties are lost, and every hand could be your last. Set in a smoky noir-inspired 1930s underworld, this joint ain’t run by mobsters... birds with sharp suits and cold hearts are the ones calling the shots.

This is just a small sample of what the full version of The Golden Caravan will offer in its full version.

2 distinct Casino Floors.

30+ Trinkets with unique effects

3 Progression shops

10+ weapons to use

Unlimited playtime!!

You walk the streets as Charlie Colombo, a slick pigeon with more guts than sense. When his grandfather Carlo Colombo, a respected locksmith, is kidnapped and dragged into the infamous Golden Caravan Casino, Charlie has no other choice but to step back into the world of rigged games, feathered crime lords, and debts paid in blood.

SATISFYING POKER-BASED COMBAT

'Round these parts, battles are fought at the Poker Table!

Play Poker Hands to deal damage, gain armor, heal up and even stun your opponents.




GAME-CHANGING TRINKETS

The Slots whisper promises... One pull, and you’re hooked.

Hit the Slot Machines scattered through the casino to earn Trinkets that offer unique effects and gameplay twists.




ENGAGING ROGUELITE PROGRESSION

Climb your way to the top, one favor at a time.

Your Allies will give you Weapons, teach you Tricks and provide you other Permanent Upgrades... at a price.

NOIR-INSPIRED 1930s ATMOSPHERE

Cigarette smoke, jazz in the background, neon lights flickering over rain-soaked streets… 

The Golden Caravan it’s a place you enter chasing fortune… and leave only if luck still remembers your name.




A GAME OF PAYBACK

Every hand hides a motive... this one’s revenge. 

Find whoever kidnapped your grandfather, uncover the truth behind The Golden Caravan, and maybe… just maybe… the House won't win this time.

text:

Follow billy
Add To Collection
Submission to Miz Jam 1
Related games
Run game

Chelly and Dog, citizens of Hell, are forced into a gauntlet of high stakes Poker death matches in order to secure their rent, which was unfairly jacked up by Satan.


With her high emotional intelligence, Chelly is able to recruit monsters to her side. Using the secret technique of "cheating", these monsters can tip the scales in her favor.

Created in 48 hours for Miz Jam 1.

Source code available here: https://github.com/billymonks/monster-casino

Instructions

Monster Casino is played exclusively using the mouse and left mouse button. Cutscenes can be skipped with the space bar.

When exploring, click on the ground to walk to a location, and click on a monster to interact with them. Some monsters will challenge you to a poker battle when interacted with.

Poker battles play out similarly to standard Texas Hold 'em, with an added twist: monsters in your party can cheat to assist you during play. To activate these cheats on your turn, just click on the party member's icon on the bottom-left corner of the screen. When you hover the mouse over the icon a tooltip will be displayed showing your party member's ability, and how much "security alert %" the ability will cost to use. The current "security alert %" can be seen on your turn on the top-right corner of the screen, designated by a yellow "!". If an ability would bring this alert level above 100%, you will be unable to use the ability.

Texas Hold 'em basics

Aside from that, battles play out like standard Texas Hold 'em. The objective of the game is to bankrupt your opponent by betting on who has the stronger hand.

Each player receives two cards (known as "hole cards", which are hidden from the other player. Five additional cards are placed on the table, known as "community cards". A player's hand value is calculated from the strongest possible 5 card hand from that player's hole cards and the community cards.

Game flow

Each turn, player and opponent take turns betting as cards are revealed.

First, before any cards have been dealt, one player pays the "small blind", and the other pays the "big blind". This money goes into the "pot". The pot is a pile of money on the table that is at stake for the current hand.

Next, each player is dealt their two hole cards and are given the opportunity to bet.

Next turn, 3 of the 5 community cards are revealed. Both player have an opportunity to bet.

Next, an additional community card is revealed and both players have another opportunity to bet.

Next, the last community card is revealed and both players get one last chance to bet.

Finally, if neither player has folded, it's time for the showdown. Both players' hole cards are revealed, and the player with the strongest hand wins the pot.

After each hand, the price of the big blind and small blind doubles, and which player is paying the big blind or small blind, and who plays first each turn (known as the dealer) switches.

Betting

Each turn, each player has the opportunity to increase the stakes, match the stakes, or fold and give up the pot. The player's options are: "Check" (if both players are currently betting the same stakes, checking passes your turn without betting any additional money.), "Call" (place money into the pot to match the opponent's stake and stay in the current hand), "Fold" (surrender the pot to the other player, ending the current hand and not placing any more money into the pot), or "Raise" (to match the opponent's stake, and bet additional money in the pot. If the opponent would like to stay in the current hand, they will have to "Call" your additional bet, or else surrender the pot.)

Hand strength from strongest to weakest
Name	Description	Example
Royal Flush	A straight flush from 10 to Ace	

Straight Flush	A straight of the same suit	
Four of a kind	Four cards of the same value	
Full house	Three of a kind and a pair	
Flush	Five cards of the same suit	
Straight	Five cards in sequential order	
Three of a kind	Three cards of the same value	
Two pairs	Two sets of pairs	
Pair	Two cards with the same value	


In the case that the player and opponent have the same hand, the hand with the higher value will win. (Example: a pair of Kings will beat a pair of Queens. If both players have the same pair, the tie will be split by who has the highest value card in their hand outside that pair.)

In the event that both players have an identically valued hand, the pot will be split among both.

Royal Flush — 10, J, Q, K, A of the same suit.

Full House — Three cards of the same rank + a pair (e.g., three kings and two fives).
Flush — Five cards of the same suit, not in sequence.
Straight — Five consecutive cards, any suit.
Three of a Kind — Three cards of the same rank (e.g., three eights).
Two Pair — Two pairs of cards of the same rank (e.g., two aces and two fours).
One Pair — Two cards of the same rank (e.g., two queens).

Definitely Poker is a card game 'definitely' similar to your average round of video poker! You are tasked with forming better hands than the dealer to win by replacing your unwanted cards!


In this game's case however! The cards that are possible to be pulled from as your replacements are revealed to you ahead of time, and can even be manipulated to prevent the drawing of certain suits outright! Guaranteeing the quality of your hands if you're clever enough to follow along.

There's also the added PRESSURE of a target goal of cash you have to reach within a certain number of rounds, health points to manage, cute girls to gaze upon (okay - ONE cute girl...). There are just a decent number of extra things to think about on top of the regular poker gameplay! I do hope you'll manage!!!


This game essentially serves as sequel/remake to a previous work of mine: 'Probably Poker'. That game was still one of my early ones, so looking back - it is a bit overly simple and uninteresting to a point. Therefore! I have gone and made something I can deem to be 'more interesting'! What do you think?

Dude, I lost my pants is a Texas Hold 'em poker and queer interactive fiction game in one. You play Rob: a hero trying to help his friend Jade recover his pants from a big night out.

page_title: Mahjong Efficiency Trainer by Euophrys
text:
View all by Euophrys
Follow Euophrys
Add To Collection
Related games
Run trainer

NEW: Source Code - Help out with translating this to new languages!
You can see a video of a strong player talking through his thoughts at this link.


This is a tile efficiency trainer for Japanese (Riichi) Mahjong. It could work for some other forms of Mahjong, but won't recognize any yaku/fan that aren't in Japanese Mahjong, so it will be somewhat inaccurate.

For every possible discard, the trainer will check how many tiles the resulting hand could draw to improve its shanten (distance from ready). If you discard a tile that isn't the best option, it will tell you the difference in efficiency. The drill completes when the hand reaches ready.

Note that playing simply for efficiency is not the optimal way to play Mahjong. It can make you easier to read. Defense is much more important. Going for high value hands often requires going against efficiency. There are many articles online that can elaborate on this. But, knowing how much efficiency you're giving up can help you better assess whether it's worth going for. This reddit comment has more info.


Settings

Tiles Allowed - This lets you remove certain suits from the wall.  The less suits, the less obvious the correct discard will generally be.
Three player rules - This removes the 2 through 8 of characters from the wall and prevents you from having the North wind as your seat wind, as if you were playing three player.
Red Fives - This adds the provided number of red fives to the wall. They are added in the order dots -> characters -> bamboo. If you have a suit removed, the red fives in that suit will also be removed and not be replaced, so having red fives set to 3 while having bamboo disabled will result in 2 red fives.
Verbose tile names - If enabled, tiles will be displayed in text as "(number) of (suit)", like "one of bamboo". If disabled, they will be written in shorthand, "(number)(character representing suit)", like "1s". "m" is for characters (manzu), "s" is for bamboo (souzu), and "p" is for circles (pinzu).
Concise history - Strips down the history output to something like "Discard: 1p (36 tiles). Best: 9m, with 38 tiles. Draw: 5s." Less clear for new players, but is easier to skim.
Show what the best option was - If enabled, the Hand History will name what the optimal tile was. As this will usually still be the optimal tile on the next draw, it can make the drill easier, if more informative.
Shuffle discarded tiles back into the wall after starting a new hand - If disabled, your hand will be added to the discard pile when generating a new one. The new hand will come from the tiles remaining in the wall. This can make the exercise harder, as there's more information to consider.
Simulate other players discarding tiles - If enabled, every time you discard a tile, three more tiles will be discarded from the wall. This gives more information to consider. Note that the ghost players don't have hands.
Consider exception hands - Allows the shanten calculation to consider Kokushi and Chiitoitsu. Chiitoitsu is a special hand made up of seven pairs, and Kokushi is a special hand made up of one of each terminal and honor with a pair of any. These hands tend to be slow to build so this option lets you ignore them without getting told you're being inefficient.
Sort hand - Whether to display the hand sorted. Uncheck this to practice reading unsorted hands.

Loading A Hand

To load a hand, enter a text representation of the hand. Enter all the values of the tiles in a suit, then a letter representing the suit, and repeat for all suits.

For Character tiles, use the letter "m" for man, "w" for wan, or "c" for characters/cracks.
For Bamboo tiles, use the letter "s" for sou, or "b" for bamboo.
For Circle tiles, use the letter "p" for pin.
For Honor tiles, use "z" or "h" for honors.
The Honor tiles are ordered, from 1 to 7, East, South, West, North, White, Green, Red.
Red fives are represented by a 0. A 0 in the Honor suit is invalid.
To specify the drawn tile or dora indicator, enter a number between 0 and 37, where 0~9 are characters, 10~19 are circles, 20~29 are bamboo, and 31~37 are the honors.
Follow this number with "t" for the drawn tile (tsumo).
Follow this number with "d" for the dora indicator.
To specify the round and seat winds, enter a number between 1 and 4, followed by "j" for the seat wind (jikaze), or by "r" or "b" for the round wind (bakaze).

For example, 340m778s236677p55z. The order of the suits doesn't matter, and you can have as few or as many as you want. Any invalid characters will be ignored, so a string like "345 man 778 sou 236677 pin 55 honor" would also (coincidentally) work, as all the extra letters don't represent suits. If you provide a hand with fewer than 14 tiles, tiles will be added at random to fill it. A hand with more than 14 tiles will result in only the last 14 tiles appearing. A hand with more than 4 of a tile will only have 4 of that tile.


See Also

Tenhou's Efficiency Calculator

Tile Efficiency: Basics by Reach Mahjong of New York
Daina Chiba's Riichi Book I chapter 2 for strategies on tile efficiency
Mahjong Fundamentals 3: Basic Tile Efficiency by The Mahjong Guide
The Japanese Mahjong Wiki's page on Shanten

The original open-source Mahjong Solitaire game powering many Mahjong experiences on the web.

If you like it, please consider to rate it, thanks :) 

Have fun!




📖 About

The goal is to remove all tiles in open pairs from the game board. 

Open: A tile is open if there are no tiles to its left, right or above it. 


Pair: Two tiles with identical front. 


Within the flowers and seasons, any two tiles from the same group can be matched.


Select two matching tiles to remove them. 


Because there are more than two tiles for each potential pairing, strategy is involved.




✨Features

🧩 84 built-in boards - from classic layouts like Turtle and Dragon to unique custom designs

🌱 Random seed based board generator  - enter or generate a custom seed to share or replay a specific randomly generated board for endless replayability

🎨 13 tile image sets - switch between beautiful tile designs in light and dark styles

🖼️ Massive visual customization - 8 image backgrounds, 375 pattern backgrounds, light/dark mode, 14 color themes

🏆 3 difficulty levels - from relaxed casual play to expert-level challenge 

🧘 Zen mode - hide the UI  for a clean, distraction-free playing experience

Sparrow Solitaire takes the classic tile-matching puzzle game mahjong solitaire, and reimagines it from the ground-up for Playdate. With simple rules and plenty of customizable options, the game is accessible to both new players and veterans of the genre.


Watch our launch trailer!

Purchase here on Itch or Panic's Catalog, or try our free demo available at the bottom of this page. Play stats from the demo carry over to the full game!

   








The goal of the game is to clear the layout by matching pairs of free tiles together. Free tiles are those which don't have any tile on top of them and whose left and right sides are unblocked. In a traditional 144 tile layout, there are 42 different tile faces: 34 normal tiles with four copies each, 4 unique “season” tiles that match with each other (black dots in corner), and 4 unique “flower” tiles that match with each other (white dots in corner).

Need more help? The game includes a full tutorial and in-game manual. Want even more tips? Check out the Playdate Wiki page.

 








We wanted to create a definitive version of mahjong solitaire, exceeding the best computer and console ports. It has all gameplay functionality you would expect, such as undo, redo, and hint functions, and way more. Shake the Playdate to reshuffle the tiles if you're stuck (only once per game!). Play layouts using the Shisen-Sho ruleset or compete head-to-head against a friend in 2-player challenge. Don't know which layout to play? Attempt the Daily Layout and share your scores via QR code.

 








Our tilesets were drawn from scratch with the Playdate’s screen in mind and they look beautiful on the device. In addition, the crank has several customizable functions: it can snap the cursor to the nearest free tile, zoom the screen, or undo and redo moves. Although mahjong games often rely on mouse or touch input, we spent a lot of time on our D-pad controls so that the cursor snapping feels intuitive, fast, and smooth.







The game includes 13 tilesets, 25 backgrounds, 208 layouts, 10 music tracks, and several gameplay and accessibility options to customize your experience.  We also included an advanced built-in editor for creating and sharing layouts with the community, and have dynamic asset loading capability so you can load in your own backgrounds or tileset designs!

   








Check out the pause screen to track your best times, scores, and win rate per-layout or across all layouts.  View a detailed overview of your stats by pressing B on a layout in the layout select.


 








Immense care has gone into everything from cursor movement to on-device performance and loading times. We have thoughtful animations and transitions for nearly everything, and the game has been thoroughly playtested. We also ensure every tile deal in Classic mode is solvable.

ABOUT AZUMANGA DONJARA DAIOH DX

The gang is back for more Donjara action! Join Osaka, Sakaki, and friends playing a modern reimagining of the 2002 Playstation cult classic. Featuring an updated Donjara NEO ruleset, try and assemble powerful tile combinations to steal your opponents points.

This version is jammed packed with a full donjara tutorial, adorable fan-art gallery, and a brand new visual style featuring tiles designed by ratpower!

Azumanga Donjara Daioh DX should work for both desktop and mobile devices with mouse or touch controls. Please note since it is built in Godot you must use a web browser with SharedBufferArray support like Chrome.

Windows and Linux versions also available for download below.

---

BASIC DONJARA RULES

Make three groups of three tiles before your opponents to win the round. You must call RIICHI before being able to win, but doing so means you're no longer allowed to change you hand shape. You can only STEAL tiles from the player to your right hand side, unless it is the tile you need to win the game by calling DONJARA.

Each hand combination is worth a different number of points based on theme and rarity, so be sure to read the YAKU LIST in game. The player with the most points after 8 rounds is declared the winner.

Want to learn more? Check out the full tutorial is available within the game!

---

LEGAL STUFF

Azumanga Donjara Daioh is a nonprofit fan project created in 2025. Azumanga Daioh is trademarked by Kiyohiko Azuma/Mediaworks. Donjara is trademarked by Bandai. Lawyers please be nice to me, this is a passion project!

Choose between a quick and essential tutorial that will cover the basic rules and mechanics of Mahjong, and a slightly longer, more detailed tutorial that will also go over a bit of the context and symbolism of the game and tiles, along with a quickplay mode for practice.

Mahjong is probably one of the most played tabletop games in the world, yet it's somewhat veiled to much of the Western and English speaking population. Most online Mahjong clients have very primitive tutorials that assumes a basic knowledge of how to play, and video tutorials tend to be short and dry, and don't do justice to this unique game that can be full of quirks and oddities.

If you don't know how to play Mahjong but you're curious about this classic game and would like to learn how, give this game a try and perhaps you will love Mahjong too!

R Mahjong - 強力AI搭載の四人麻雀

R Mahjong is the best riichi mahjong application for mobile devices. Why is this so? To understand this, it is necessary to consider the shortcomings of existing riichi mahjong applications. Most of these applications have frankly weak AI. Playing against such “AI” is simply not interesting, and such applications are only suitable for learning the mechanics of the game and the rules of riichi mahjong. As a matter of fact, the authors of these applications do not hide this (numerous built-in manuals (in fact, rules) for playing riichi mahjong are evidence of this).


However, those players who have “mastered” mahjong in this way will try to play against other players, for example on tenhou or mahjongsoul, will be bitterly disappointed. And the point is not at all that they will face strong opponents there.


It turns out that knowing the rules is not enough. It is necessary to study the strategy of playing mahjong, understand its principles and change your psychology, aiming not at winning in each game (this is impossible), but to maximize the efficiency of the game, maximizing the probability and magnitude of winning and minimizing the probability and magnitude of loss.


And, of course, in addition to studying theory, you need to practice playing against strong opponents. This is where the R Mahjong app can reach its potential. Equipped with unprecedentedly strong (for mobile devices) AI, the R Mahjong application allows the player to gain a gaming experience almost impossible to achieve before. Previously, AI of comparable strength was only available on PC (爆打 created by Naoki Mizukami).


What is this “previously unavailable gaming experience”?

First of all, the player immediately gets three strong opponents to play against, which are REALLY more interesting than playing against a weak "AI" (or weak players in a lower-level lobby). 
Second, the player has unlimited time to think about each move.
Third, playing against strong opponents will give the player the necessary game experience to become stronger.
Fourth, playing against three strong and stable opponents, which are AI will allow the player to evaluate his game progress more easily and accurately than when playing against human players.
Fifth, R Mahjong has a training mode in which the player can see the tiles in their opponents' hands and receive hints from the AI, allowing the player to not only see how the AI makes decisions, but also mimic it. It also teaches the player to read the discard of the opponents.

The system for collecting and displaying game statistics in R Mahjong is also designed to help the player become stronger. This system is virtually unparalleled.

And it's not just that almost every aspect of the game can be analyzed. Statistics are available not only for the player, but also for his opponents. A comparative analysis of statistics will allow the player to timely identify and correct statistical imbalances in his game. 

In addition to the single-player mode of playing against AI, the R Mahjong application has a multiplayer mode (on a local network via Wi-Fi). Moreover, you can play in this mode with any number of human players. Missing players will be replaced by AI. 

Of course, R Mahjong also has the ability to record and play step-by-step games played, and viewing is available from the point any player's view. 

And finally, last but not least. R Mahjong app is completely free. 

R Mahjong application is created to help the player become stronger, and get more and more pleasure from riichi mahjong - this wonderful game.

YONJONG!

Welcome to the world of "YONJONG!", where cute cats and intense brain battles meet! 🐱🀄

 Experience a new style of Mahjong that is simple to learn but hard to master. Immerse yourself in a beautiful Japanese atmosphere with soothing music and traditional aesthetics.

🔥 The Unique "Stock Rule"

Unlike traditional Mahjong, "Yonjang!" is played with only 4 tiles in hand. But there's a twist! We introduced the "Stock System." You can keep one extra tile in your stock slot and swap it with your drawn tile at any time.

However, your stocked tile is fully visible to your opponents! Do you keep a safe tile for defense, or hold onto a dangerous tile for a high-scoring hand? Use the stock to read your opponents or bluff them! The choice is yours.

✨ Key Features:

Simple & Deep: With only 5 tiles to complete a hand (3-tile meld + pair), games are fast-paced and exciting. Perfect for short breaks!

Online & Friend Matches: Battle players nationwide in Ranked Matches to climb the leaderboards, or set up a Private Room with a password to play with friends! (Smart AI cats will automatically join if you are short on players).

Japanese Aesthetics: Enjoy the relaxing visuals and sounds inspired by shrines, cherry blossoms, and traditional Japan.

Customization & Omikuji: Spend your cat coins at the shop to draw an Omikuji (Fortune) and collect unique avatars, tile skins, and table mats to show off your style!

English Support: Fully playable in English (Switch via the flag icon on the title screen).

🎮 How to Play:

Draw a tile.

Swap it with your Stock tile if needed.

Discard a tile to keep your hand at 4 tiles.

Aim for a winning hand (Run/Triplet + Pair) and declare "Ron" or "Tsumo"!

---

Weary from a day of travel, you make camp in the woods. Yet before your can drift off to sleep you're ambushed by goblins. As their hostage, there's only one way to earn your freedom, beating them at their own game.

Goblin Dice is a reverse roguelike blackjack style game played with a set of 6 dice. Use your spells to manipulate the totals and cheat your way to victory, at least until the goblins get frustrated.

Defeat 16 semi-randomized opponents to earn your freedom and pick up a pile of Goblin Bucks in the process. Though you're not sure of any stores that accept them as legal tender.

Simple but fun Blackjack card game.

Rules:

The goal of blackjack is to beat the dealer's hand without going over 21.
Face cards are worth 10. Aces are worth 1 or 11, whichever makes a better hand.
Each player starts with two cards, one of the dealer's cards is hidden until the end.
To 'Hit' is to ask for another card. To 'Stand' is to hold your total and end your turn.
If you go over 21 you bust, and the dealer wins regardless of the dealer's hand.
If you are dealt 21 from the start (Ace & 10), you got a blackjack.
Blackjack usually means you win 1.5 the amount of your bet. Depends on the casino.
Dealer will hit until his/her cards total 17 or higher.
Doubling is like a hit, only the bet is doubled and you only get one more card.
Split can be done when you have two of the same card - the pair is split into two hands.
Splitting also doubles the bet, because each new hand is worth the original bet.
You can only double/split on the first move, or first move of a hand created by a split.
You cannot play on two aces after they are split.
You can double on a hand resulting from a split, tripling or quadrupling you bet.

Add To Collection
Related games
C64 Green Felt Classics

Three classics  Solitaire, Yahtzee and Blackjack reissued as new BASIC V2 type-in listings for the extra nostalgic experience.

All three games have in common to make use of the rarely seen ECM (=Extended Color Mode). In this mode each character can have one of 4 different background colors. This is great in e.g. card games to allow the symbols on the cards having a white background while the overall background can remain green. The downside of this mode is, that only a total of 64 characters can be displayed at a time, which is the main reason why we don't see this mode more often. But using ECM wisely, brings a complete new and fresh look into C64 games.


Please note that Solitaire requires a 1351 Commodore™ mouse to play (in Joystick Port 2). These mice became rare and are nowadays hard to find to buy for a reasonable price. However, there are much cheaper adapters you can get in combination with an old PS2 mouse.  Or you can just play in the VICE emulator where you can use your standard PC mouse to control the mouse pointer (1351 mouse needs to be enabled in the settings). Alternatively there is some replacement code on the last page of the PDF listing to make a Joystick controlled version out of it.

The other two games Yahtzee and Blackjack  are controlled by keyboard.

Why as type-in listing and not as executable?

Because I would like you to experience my creations in a different way. See it like putting together a LEGO™ model, where the assembling is half the fun. And the side effect is - without knowing - you learn a bit of BASIC coding on the way and may spot some of my tricks to make the slow BASIC V2 a little bit faster. And likewise LEGO™ you can re-use parts of the listing's code in your own creations.

Don't worry about losing time finding typos. The listings come with a checksum tool, so you have quick feedback - per line - to see, if you typed the statements in correctly. 

And now I hope you will enjoy the forgotten magic of typing in cryptic statements and seeing a running game coming out in the end.
